title: Free printable ADHD cleaning checklist (one-page PDF, no email)
description: Free printable ADHD cleaning checklist: six room resets with timers, a bad-day line for each, and a daily bare minimum. One-page PDF, direct download, no email.

faq.q: Is the ADHD cleaning checklist really free?
faq.a: Yes. The PDF link on this page is a direct download. No email, no checkout, no trial. It is one A4 page and prints on any home printer.

Six resets with a timer each: kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, living room, laundry from basket to drawer, and one doom pile. Every reset ends with a shaded bad-day line, the single step that still counts on a day you cannot function. A daily bare-minimum block sits at the bottom.

faq.q: How is this different from a normal cleaning checklist?
faq.a: Three ways. Every task is sized in minutes you can measure, not in rooms. Every reset has a bad-day version, so the list never asks for more than you have. And the timer is the stop signal: you finish when it rings, not when the room is done.

faq.q: Do I need an ADHD diagnosis to use it?
faq.a: No. It is built for anyone whose brain stalls on starting boring tasks or holding a multi-step job in mind. Nothing on it is medical advice and none of it needs a label to work.

jsonld_extra.name: How to use the ADHD cleaning checklist

step.name: Print it
step.text: Download the one-page PDF and print it on plain A4 or letter paper. Stick it where the mess is, not in a drawer.

step.name: Pick one reset
step.text: Choose the room that bothers you most when you walk in. Ignore the rest of the sheet.

step.name: Set the timer
step.text: Set the timer printed next to that reset, 5 to 15 minutes, and start with the first line.

step.name: Stop when it rings
step.text: When the timer rings you are done, even mid-task. Tick what you did. Leave the rest.

step.name: On a bad day, do the shaded line
step.text: If you cannot start, do only the bad-day line in one room and call the day done. It counts.
